subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for November 23, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

script.heading: Story 3 - Intraoperative peripheral perfusion index and mortality after
sentences: Story 3 is about Intraoperative peripheral perfusion index and mortality after noncardiac surgery: a retrospective cohort study..
This is a cohort study from British journal of anaesthesia.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in adults (≥18 yr) undergoing general anaesthesia for noncardiac surgery, how should we interpret exposure, 1185 (0.6%) in the lower half of exposed procedures, and 5227 (2.6%) in the upper half (split at 3.8 PI⋅min) compared with no exposure, the adjusted odds ratio for 30-day mortality was 2.18 (95% CI 1.98-2.40, overall association P<0.001) at th?

Among 399 842 patients undergoing 540 101 procedures, a total of 7066 (1.3%) deaths occurred within 30 days: 654 (0.5%) among procedures with no exposure, 1185 (0.6%) in the lower half of exposed procedures, and 5227 (2.6%) in the upper half (split at 3.8 PI⋅min).

Compared with no exposure, the adjusted odds ratio for 30-day mortality was 2.18 (95% CI 1.98-2.40, overall association P<0.001) at the 95th percentile of exposure (42.5 PI⋅min), with similar patterns observed across the major surgical specialties.
For the composite outcome, the corresponding odds ratio was 1.16 (95% CI 1.14-1.18; P<0.001).
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Useful for risk stratification and hypothesis generation, but avoid causal bedside changes unless supported by interventional evidence.
Useful English phrase: these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the details of design and applicability matter.

script.heading: Outro
sentences: That wraps up today's journal club style update.
Before applying any finding, check the full source, the absolute effect size, and your local ICU context.
For English practice, repeat one academic phrase from each article out loud.

articles.title: Antimicrobial stewardship and resistance in intensive care units in the UK: a prospective national audit.
articles.summary: Subsequently, we collected longitudinal data on review of therapy and antimicrobial resistance in a subset of patients who had commenced therapy within the previous 3 days. We studied 2626 patients from 154/292 (52.7%) ICUs. Antimicrobial therapy was prescribed in 1592 (60.6%) patients. Of 2116 empiric antimicrobial orders, 1592 (75.2%) were compliant with unit-level guidelines. For non-compliant orders, 253 (12.0% of all empiric orders) were discussed with infection specialists and 69 (3.3%) provided justification for off-guidance therapy, but 202 (9.5%) were prescribed outside guidance without justification or discussion with infection specialists.

articles.title: Intraoperative peripheral perfusion index and mortality after noncardiac surgery: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.summary: The secondary outcome was a 30-day composite of postoperative intensive care unit admission, reoperation, acute kidney injury, or prolonged hospital stay. Among 399 842 patients undergoing 540 101 procedures, a total of 7066 (1.3%) deaths occurred within 30 days: 654 (0.5%) among procedures with no exposure, 1185 (0.6%) in the lower half of exposed procedures, and 5227 (2.6%) in the upper half (split at 3.8 PI⋅min). Compared with no exposure, the adjusted odds ratio for 30-day mortality was 2.18 (95% CI 1.98-2.40, overall association P<0.001) at the 95th percentile of exposure (42.5 PI⋅min), with similar patterns observed across the major surgical specialties. For the composite outcome, the corresponding odds ratio was 1.16 (95% CI 1.14-1.18; P<0.001). Intraoperative haemodynamic monitoring primarily targets arterial pressure and flow but might not adequately reflect tissue perfusion.
